PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY-CLIENT / WORK PRODUCT
GAP ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM - Protocol PTX-4820-201 v3.0 (May 18, 2025) vs. FDA requirements and April 2, 2025 Pre-IND minutes
To: S. Kowalski (Pinnacle). From: HSL. Target IND date: Sept 15, 2025. Review is of the Protocol and Appendix A ICF only (not CMC, pharm/tox, IB).

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Protocol is not ready for IND submission. Six of the seven FDA Pre-IND action items (minutes Sec. 6, item 1(a)-(f)) are unimplemented or only partly implemented, although Protocol Sec. 2.1 states the recommendations "have been incorporated... where appropriate" - a statement FDA will see is inaccurate. The minutes warn that no DSMB commitment "could contribute to a clinical hold" (21 CFR 312.42). Beyond the minutes: no pregnancy/contraception provisions; ICF gaps; a sample-size error leaving ~50% power; no IND safety-report timelines; no Part 11 or Health Canada provisions; and an outdated no-approved-therapy statement. The internal draft Regulatory Requirements Checklist cannot be delivered as is (Sec. 5). Items are remediable by Sept 15 if Trident starts now; sequence DSMB charter, SAP and ICF first.

Severity key: Critical = likely clinical hold, refuse-to-file or reviewer rejection of the primary endpoint; Major = probable FDA/IRB comment or deficiency letter; Minor = clean-up.

2. FINDINGS (Protocol section -> authority -> remediation)

CRITICAL
C-1 DSMB discretionary (Sec. 9.4: "may be convened at the Sponsor's discretion... If convened"). Minutes 4.4: DSMB "not optional"; mandatory language; operational and charter final before first subject; hepatologist, independent biostatistician, clinical pharmacologist; review after first 90 subjects (~25%), at interim, on signals, ad hoc; authority over dose changes, arm termination, enrollment suspension; Sponsor commitment to consider recommendations. Protocol has none of these; Sec. 10.3 shares interim results with the DSMB "(if convened)". Fix: replace Sec. 9.4 with "A DSMB will be established and operational before the first subject is randomized," with the composition, schedule, authority and charter-as-appendix terms above. Authority: minutes 4.4; 21 CFR 312.42; 21 CFR 312.56(d).
C-2 No study-level stopping criteria. Sec. 9.5 has only individual-subject rules (ALT >10x ULN; Hy's Law; anaphylaxis; pregnancy). Hepatic decompensation events (variceal bleeding, ascites, any-grade encephalopathy, hepatorenal syndrome) are only AESIs (Sec. 9.2(5)); no threshold triggers DSMB review. Minutes 4.5 example: >=2 events in any arm or significant active-vs-placebo imbalance triggers expedited unscheduled DSMB review; thresholds fixed in protocol and charter pre-enrollment. Fix: add Sec. 9.5.2 with those triggers. Related: FDA recommends LFTs every 2 weeks for 12 weeks then monthly; Table 4 has Weeks 2, 4, 8, 12 then 4-6 weekly. Add Weeks 6 and 10 and monthly testing.
C-3 Interim analysis. Sec. 10.3: single efficacy interim at Week 26 of the last enrolled subject (about April 2027, when most subjects have finished); no futility analysis. Minutes 4.6: interim at 50% enrollment (~180 randomized); formal futility analysis, conditional power <20% as threshold; arm-level drop or study termination authority to the DSMB; independent statistician under a firewall; all rules prespecified in SAP/charter before first subject and not changed without notice to FDA. The Protocol also contradicts itself (Week 26 of last subject vs "if... approximately 50%", nominal alpha ~0.003). A true O'Brien-Fleming boundary at 50% information is roughly 0.005 two-sided - confirm with the biostatistician. Fix: revise Sec. 10.3; limit "authorized Sponsor personnel" access to results. FDA accepted O'Brien-Fleming (agreed).
C-4 Central pathology. Sec. 8.1 uses one central pathologist, calibrated with "the Sponsor's medical team" (a blinding risk), with 10% re-read. Minutes 4.1: strongly recommended panel of at least two independent hepatopathologists, third adjudicator, single-reader assessment called "unacceptable inter-reader variability"; prespecify qualifications, blinding (treatment, visit, other readers), disagreement definition (any fibrosis-stage discordance or NAS difference >=2), adjudication method, and training/calibration. Fix: rewrite Sec. 8.1 and SAP; remove Sponsor-team calibration.
C-5 Reproductive safety. No pregnancy test, contraception requirement, or WOCBP/male-partner provisions anywhere (Sec. 4, 6, Table 4), yet Sec. 4.3/9.5.1 treat pregnancy as a stopping event and the Protocol is a 52-week trial of a novel peptide with unestablished reproductive toxicity (minutes 4.7 ask for any completed reproductive tox data). ICH M3(R2): WOCBP not on highly effective contraception or of unknown pregnancy status should not be enrolled before female reproduction toxicity studies and the genotoxicity battery are completed; precautions include pregnancy testing, highly effective contraception and entry after a confirmed menstrual period. Fix: add serum beta-hCG at screening/Day 1 and urine tests at each visit through follow-up, highly effective contraception through 12+ weeks after last dose, pregnancy follow-up procedure, exclusion of pregnant/lactating women; confirm status of EFD studies with Dr. Chen (not verified by us).
C-6 ICF omissions (21 CFR 50.25; Appendix A). Missing: (a)(5) confidentiality and possibility of FDA inspection of records; (a)(6) compensation/medical treatment for injury (Protocol Sec. 13.4 has insurance but the ICF is silent); (b)(1) unforeseeable risks to embryo/fetus; (b)(5) significant new findings; and 50.25(c) - the verbatim ClinicalTrials.gov statement ("A description of this clinical trial will be available on http://www.ClinicalTrials.gov, as required by U.S. Law...") for an applicable clinical trial; Protocol Sec. 13.6 commits to registration. Partial: (b)(3) additional costs, (b)(4) consequences of withdrawal/orderly termination, (a)(1) procedures (see M-4). Fix: insert required text.

MAJOR
M-1 Titration. Table 3/Sec. 5.2: Arm C reaches 30 mg at Week 3 (5/15/30). Minutes 4.2 and action item 1(b): at least 4 weeks (e.g., 5, 10, 15, then 30 mg). Revise Table 3, ICF, pharmacy materials, and add GI dose-delay/reduction rules (partly in Sec. 9.5.1). Arm B 1-week titration is optional per FDA.
M-2 MELD. Sec. 4.2(2) excludes only "history" of decompensation. Add exclusion: MELD >=15 at screening (minutes 4.3; action item 1(c)), keeping the clinical criteria. Add washout for high-dose acetaminophen.
M-3 Misstatement of current therapy. Sec. 2.1 and ICF A5 say no FDA-approved pharmacotherapy exists for NASH with fibrosis. Rezdiffra (resmetirom) received FDA accelerated approval on March 14, 2024 for noncirrhotic NASH with F2-F3 fibrosis (Madrigal press release, per search). This undercuts the ICF alternatives disclosure (50.25(a)(4)), the placebo-control rationale, and the orphan-need narrative. Revise text, ICF alternatives, and placebo-justification. Note the FDA NASH guidance (Nov/Dec 2018) is, per our search, still a draft; the Protocol should not describe it as final guidance.
M-4 ICF duration error. ICF A2 says "approximately 12 months." Protocol: 52 weeks treatment + 12 weeks follow-up = 64 weeks from randomization; 72 weeks including up to 8 weeks of screening (Sec. 5.1). Correction to the email thread: 64 weeks is about 14.8 months, not 16; about 16.5 months is the 72-week figure. ICF should state both. ICF also does not describe the three follow-up visits, PK sampling, or MRI-PDFF/genotype activities (Protocol 3.3 lists PNPLA3 genotyping and MRI-PDFF subset but neither appears in Table 4 or the ICF - add optional separate consent or delete). Visit payment: $150 x 17 = $2,550 but Sec. 13.4 counts 17 visits "Day 1 through Week 64," which is 16 visits (17 including screening) - reconcile.
M-5 IND safety reporting (Sec. 9.1). Sponsor reporting is stated only "as required by applicable law." 21 CFR 312.32(c): 15 calendar days for serious, unexpected suspected adverse reactions (c)(1); 7 calendar days for unexpected fatal/life-threatening ones (c)(2); follow-up (c)(3). Protocol needs these, "reasonable possibility" causality standard (it uses only related/not related), expectedness vs IB, aggregate-analysis and AESI/hepatic-signal reporting, and IRB notification. Investigator SAE timeline of 48 hours to sponsor is acceptable but should be shortened to 24 hours to preserve the sponsor's 7-day clock for fatal/life-threatening events (recommendation). (Rated Major, not Critical, because sponsor duties exist regardless of protocol text.)
M-6 Sample size. Sec. 10.1: 30% vs 45%, 80% power, two-sided 0.05 gives 162 evaluable per arm by the standard two-proportion formula (our calculation), not 78; with 15% attrition about 191 randomized per arm (about 760 total), before any multiplicity penalty. At 78 evaluable per arm, power is about 50%. FDA called the assumptions "generally reasonable" (minutes Sec. 5) but did not check the arithmetic. Also mITT excludes anyone without a Week 52 biopsy, so the 15% dropout allowance may be low. Fix before IND: re-derive, or restate objectives (Phase 2b dose-ranging, estimation-focused) and state a justified alternative. Underpowered design is a hold ground for Phase 2 under 312.42(b)(2) ("clearly deficient in design"; section paragraph numbering from memory - verify). Add an ICH E9(R1) estimand (minutes Sec. 5).
M-7 21 CFR Part 11 / EDC (Sec. 12.1). TrialVault (Trident's proprietary EDC) is described with password roles only; no statement on validation, computer-generated time-stamped audit trails, electronic signatures (11.50/11.70/11.100), backup, or blinding safeguards, though minutes Sec. 5 expressly require Part 11 compliance and validated EDC with audit trails. Add a Part 11 section and obtain Trident's validation summary.
M-8 Canada. Sec. 2.2 and 13.1 cite only FDA/ICH; Sec. 11.2 says only "local" REB arrangements. Add Health Canada Food and Drug Regulations Part C, Division 5 (C.05.001 ff.), Clinical Trial Application (C.05.005) with the 30-day default period before sale/import for trial purposes (C.05.006), REB approval and Canadian ethical/privacy requirements; also Quebec site language and Canadian privacy law (not verified by us). Suggested Sec. 2.2 text: "Canadian sites will operate under the Food and Drug Regulations, Part C, Division 5, with Health Canada CTA authorization and REB approval documented before any Canadian site enrolls." Sec. 13.1: add CTA submission, a no-objection letter, and amendment submissions to Health Canada. Recommend Canadian counsel; note fee-estimate notice in engagement letter VI.
M-9 Nonclinical coverage for 52-week dosing. Sec. 2.1 relies on 26-week GLP studies. Minutes 4.7: 39-week non-rodent study should start before/at first dosing, with results before any subject is dosed beyond 26 weeks (about April 2026 for first enrollees). The Protocol has no stage-gate. Add a dosing-duration gate. IND cover letter commitment (action item 3) is outside Protocol scope but must be confirmed.
M-10 Human experience. Neither the Protocol nor minutes identify any human exposure to PTX-4820 (only PTX-3100); minutes call the compound one with "limited human safety data." Confirm whether a Phase 1 exists; if not, FDA may question a 52-week, 30 mg-arm first-in-human design (starting-dose/safety-margin justification, sentinel dosing). Unresolved fact question for Dr. Anand.
M-11 Misstatement of FDA alignment. Sec. 2.1 says recommendations have been incorporated. Remove or correct once items C-1 to C-4, M-1, M-2 are done. The 30-day window to dispute the minutes has closed; the minutes call the receptor "GVP" (it is GIP) - immaterial, note at next contact.

MINOR
m-1 Biopsy adequacy: Protocol requires 20 mm and 11 portal tracts, stricter than FDA's 1.5 cm/6; the extra stringency may raise inadequate-specimen rates, and Protocol lacks a repeat-biopsy procedure/time window (action item 4). m-2 Sec. 11.2 cites 45 CFR 46.114(b) for single IRB; for an FDA-regulated study cite 21 CFR 56.114 (cooperative research); confirm local IRB reliance for US sites. m-5 FibroScan at Week 24, FDA-agreed secondary endpoints list Weeks 26 and 52 - align. m-6 Protocol cites ICH E6(R2); ICH adopted E6(R3) in January 2025 (our recollection, not verified) - consider R3 wording; FDA's adoption date is not verified. m-7 Sec. 11.3 has no vulnerable-population provisions.

3. ALIGNED: primary endpoint/paired biopsy, 1:1:1:1 design, age/F4/alcohol criteria, individual ALT/Hy's Law rules, O'Brien-Fleming spending, secondary endpoints, EAC, 30-day IND wait.

4. REMEDIATION SEQUENCE
Week 1: DSMB, pathology, interim/SAP, ICF. Week 2: pregnancy, titration, MELD, safety reporting, sample size, Part 11. Week 3: Canada, nonclinical gate. Consider a Type C meeting; issue Protocol v4.0.

5. DRAFT CHECKLIST
The draft XLSX checklist conflicts with Protocol v3.0 and must be re-run before delivery: it describes 50/150/300 mg doses, Protocol v2.0 (22-Apr-2024), Ishak endpoint, ANCOVA, 24-hour SAE reporting, a different medical monitor, rat/dog toxicology, ~40 sites, three biopsies, HIPAA/genetic ICF sections and a DSMB with 90/180/270 reviews, and marks DSMB/stopping rules 'Y'. It also cites non-existent 312.23(a)(6)(iii)(h)-(m). Its WOCBP, safety-timeline, Part 11 and ICF flags are directionally right. Use the engagement letter's four-status scale.

6. LIMITS
eCFR/Cornell pages were blocked; regulatory text was confirmed via search summaries only (50.25(c), 312.32 timelines, Division 5 30-day period, M3(R2) WOCBP, Rezdiffra approval, NASH guidance draft status). Unverified: 312.42(b)(2) paragraph numbers, E6(R3) status, Quebec/Canadian privacy points, current status of EFD and 39-week toxicology studies. Do not share with Trident or Ridgeway without a privilege consult.
